project-trajectory/scripts/spine_carrier.contract: spine_carrier.py module: the requirement spine's registry CARRIER. SPINE_TABLE maps an id column to its TOML tier table (SR-ID->requirement, LLR-ID->design, TC-ID->test); SPINE_COLUMN maps a carrier key to today's COLUMN NAME and is the exact inverse of migrate_carrier.KEY. rows_from_text(text, id_col, carrier) -> {id: row} under today's column names, or None when a TOML text does not parse (absent, never empty); rows_from_toml / rows_from_csv are the two arms. carriers(rel) -> both suffixed paths, for an applicability test that must span the cutover. resolve(path) -> the live carrier file, RAISING when both exist rather than resolving by precedence; load(path, id_col) -> rows in file order, the shape csv.DictReader returns, raising on a carrier that exists and will not parse. The `-000` example filter is NOT applied here - that is trace_text's rule.
project-trajectory/scripts/spine_carrier.notes: source - spine_carrier consumes nothing by design, the trace_text pattern: text in, rows out, with resolve()'s existence check the single deliberate exception because the dual-home refusal must have one home. ONE module rather than eleven copies, which is the one admitted exception to the rejection of a shared _kitcommon: F5 buys cross-script copy-ability and was written for small stable plumbing, but a duplicated VOCABULARY fails silently rather than visibly. The consumers cell names trace as the first importer; check_trajectory imports it too, and the remaining spine readers join as they convert.

project-trajectory/scripts/migrate_carri.notes: source - reads the registries and writes beside them; consumes no kit module. It ships to adopters because every adopting repo migrates too and the round-trip proof is the migration's evidence (SR-129's 140-cell lesson). NOT one-shot, and NOT awaiting retirement: a downstream repo re-syncing onto a newer kit AFTER the carrier cutover still holds its registries on a legacy carrier, so this converter is the standing path for that conversion and has no terminus to wait for. The CSV fallback in spine_carrier does expire - once no supported baseline predates the migration - and this module does not expire with it, which is why its maturity is its own affair rather than the conversion programme's.

project-trajectory/scripts/lane.py.notes: A program-close connectivity mint: the seam was already load-bearing (the extraction that split it out is what the design's §A4.2 describes) but carried no IF row of its own, and lane.py's own docstring says so rather than paper over the drift by declaring it from the extracted half.
